Extract it into the JSON schema: - supplier = who issued the invoice; buyer = the restaurant company it was billed to. taxId = VAT/NIF/CNPJ number as printed. - date and dueDate as YYYY-MM-DD (empty string if absent). currency as an ISO code. - One entry in lines per product line, in order. Skip lines that are only totals, deposits summaries or page footers. - unitPrice is the price per invoiced unit EXCLUDING VAT when the invoice shows it; vatRate as a percentage number (e.g. 18). - packSize/packUnit: the content of one unit when printed in the description (e.g. "Olive oil 5L" -> 5, "l"; "Flour 25kg" -> 25, "kg"; "Wine 75cl" -> 0.75, "l"). Use null and "" when unknown. - ean: barcode digits if printed; code: the supplier's own product code. - genericName: a short generic ingredient name in English without brand, size or packaging (e.g. "olive oil extra virgin", "beef ribeye", "mozzarella"). For wines and drinks use the product name without the size. - category: one of produce, meat, fish, dairy, dry goods, bakery, beverages, wine, spirits, beer, cleaning, packaging, other. - Use null for numbers that are not printed; never guess totals.

Handwriting may misspell or abbreviate it (e.g. "JefFeson", "Jeferson", "Jeff", "Jef", "J.") — pick the row that best matches. Ignore every other person. nameAsWritten = the name exactly as written in the rota ("" if not found). Dates: - If the rota prints dates (header row, title like "12-17 Oct"), use them. - Otherwise columns are weekdays (M T W T F S S / Mon..Sun / Seg..Dom); map them onto the week starting Monday {WEEK_START}. weekStart = the Monday of the week you used, YYYY-MM-DD. One entry in shifts per day the worker works, Monday first: - date YYYY-MM-DD. - start/end in 24h HH:MM. "17-" or "17" or "18 -" means it starts at 17:00 and the end is not written: end = "". "11-17:00" or "11-5" means 11:00-17:00 (read pm sensibly: a restaurant shift ending at "5" after starting at "11" ends 17:00). - Days off ("Off", "OFF", "-", "—", "x", empty, "+") are NOT shifts: leave them out. - A cell with a code but no readable time (e.g. "NXR", "training", "?") → include it with start "" and end "", and explain in note. - raw = the cell text exactly as written. - note = anything useful (e.g. "code NXR, unclear", "split shift"), else "". placeGuess = the venue if you can tell it from the page (logo, letterhead, title). The worker's venues are: {PLACES}. Answer with one of these names when it matches, else the name as written, else "". notes = short remarks for the worker in Portuguese (e.g. unclear handwriting on Thursday), else "".
